function.name: chrome
function.description: Drive the user's real Chrome browser. Actions: start / stop / status (the relay this tool talks through) - ping (is the extension answering) - tabs (list open tabs) - nav (needs url, optional new_tab) - text (page text, optional css selector) - click (css selector, or x and y) - write_text (type into a field: needs text, optional selector, clear, enter) - scroll (move the page or an element: dy pixels, negative = up, or to top|bottom — when the page is longer than the viewport, scroll before re-shooting, because a second shot without a scroll shows the same pixels) - shot (screenshot the visible viewport — on a vision model the picture is attached to your next message automatically, so you see it without any extra call). A repeat shot that is byte-identical to the previous one says so and is NOT attached again. On a text-only model, read a scrollable panel (e.g. a filter modal) with text + the panel's CSS selector — it returns the panel's full innerText, below-the-fold included, no scrolling and no vision — rather than repeated shots. A connection error when nothing is running is the normal idle state, not a broken page — call action=start and retry. write_text with no selector types into whatever is focused, so click then write_text works on fields with no stable selector.

new_tab.description: nav: open in a new tab

selector.description: CSS selector for text/click/scroll (scroll: that element scrolls, not the page)

dy.description: scroll: pixels to move; negative scrolls up

to.description: scroll: jump to top or bottom

x.description: click by coordinate instead of selector

y.description: click by coordinate instead of selector

clear.description: write_text: replace the field (default true); false appends

enter.description: write_text: press Enter afterwards (submits most forms)
